title: Working on a game where you have to convince a local LLM AI model that its reality is a simulation.
author: MorphLand
selftext:
A chat sim game where every conversation is different! My game Simulation Simulator is a freeform conversation game where you try to convince your AI best friend that reality is a simulation. Runs a local LLM (Llama 3.1) entirely offline. Multiple endings! 

I think this is a really natural implementation of AI with gaming.

Wishlist Simulation Simulator on steam!

comments.author: DatabaseConstant7870
comments.body: Does the llm have access to your pc? Can you upset it and it try to attack your device

replies.author: Heralax_Tekran
replies.body: local means the files are running locally, not that it has any shell access or anything. it's bascially like a (large) program.

replies.author: MorphLand
replies.body: Nope. It’s just part of the unity game it has no access to files or anything. It’s a sophisticated NPC basically.

comments.author: ioaia
comments.body: This is a pretty clever idea. Is it possible to win ?

replies.author: MorphLand
replies.body:
Yup! 5 endings total. One secret infinite mode when you’ve unlocked them all.

Depending on how you interact, different endings become possible. For example, there’s a romance ending where he admits he’s loved you all along, there’s an ending where he admits he’s been a simulation this whole time. It’s all about finessing the robot right .

comments.author: mcidclan
comments.body: Funny and interesting one, what perf do you get on a mid range pc?

replies.author: MorphLand
replies.body: It's really good! Max amount time between responses is like 2-3 seconds when it's really cooking. Performs better in builds than in unity editor actually. I'm actually developing this on a REALLY shitty macbook so performance is pretty important.
